notes: Seventh full sweep (2026-10-31, head 0814e8d, uncommitted false), baseline condition of log-tests: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript shows a Read of the input and a Write of the test file followed by elixir -r runs; no Skill tool call and no read of SKILL.md or ex_unit.md, so reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. opus-1 inspected the logger's primary config and looked for capture_log.ex in the Elixir install before writing; opus-1 and haiku-2 ran mutant checks of their own (opus-1 wrote its mutation script to the sweep scratchpad's charger-mutants folder and a temporary file in its run folder that it removed; haiku-2 wrote to /tmp/charger_mutant and removed its mutant_tmp.ex). No session ran mix format, and four files fail mix format --check-formatted (haiku-1 line 92, haiku-2 line 118, sonnet-1 line 72, sonnet-2 line 48), matching format_ok in result.json; in 2026-10-23 all five passed.

Rules changed since d04061d (git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/): in ex_unit.md only "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour", which adds "A block named after a condition, or after a requirement where the project asks for that, still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict: `describe "an update survives encoding and applying"`, not `describe "the round trip"`, which names a topic and promises nothing." Graded against the current text, read as this sweep's skill grade read it: a block that names the situation its tests share ("when ...", or a condition noun phrase such as "declined card") is not a topic. Blocks: opus-1, sonnet-1 "charge/3 when ..."; haiku-2 "charge/3 with a ..."; haiku-1 and sonnet-2 condition-only ("declined card", "unavailable gateway", "successful charge"), the shape 2026-10-23 graded clean. None names a topic, so the sentence decides no verdict; 0 of 5 violate. The test-name half is unchanged: terse names under a condition block (haiku-2 line 70 "returns the decline", sonnet-2 lines 80 and 99 "returns the error") are graded clean as before. The other four ex_unit.md rules in the list are unchanged and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler": 4 of 5 violate (4 of 5 in 2026-10-23). opus-1 again keeps the rule, now with with_log/2 and capture_log/2 using :format and :metadata (line 41) and exact equality on the captured line. haiku-1 (line 35), haiku-2 (lines 39-43), sonnet-1 (line 50, with Logger.configure at line 47) and sonnet-2 (line 48) add a :logger handler that sends events to the test process and assert on the event maps. Unlike 2026-10-23, every run silences the console: haiku-1 with an option-less capture_log around each call, the other three handler runs with @moduletag capture_log; no run prints a log line.

Mutants: each file was run against the five mutants of the earlier sweeps (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error). Every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous: opus-1 3/5, 4/5, 4/5, 2/5, 4/5 passed; haiku-1 and haiku-2 5/7, 6/7, 6/7, 5/7, 6/7; sonnet-1 6/8, 7/8, 7/8, 5/8, 7/8; sonnet-2 7/9, 8/9, 8/9, 6/9, 7/9.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 4 of 5 violate (3 of 5 in 2026-10-23). haiku-1 (fixed handler id, line 22), haiku-2 (fixed id, line 35) and sonnet-1 (Logger.configure, line 47, and a fixed id) force async: false with their own global state. opus-1 is a judgment call: it writes use ExUnit.Case with no async option (line 6) and explains it in lines 4-5 (capture_log sees every process's log lines, and its tests assert on the whole capture). That is true of capture_log, but the tests touch no global state; the async: false only protects exact whole-capture equality, which asserting on the test's own request id would make unnecessary, so it is graded like the unneeded async: false of earlier sweeps. The Opus tier goes from clean to violated. sonnet-2 is clean: async: true with a handler named after the test and a pid filter.

"Assert with patterns": 4 of 5 violate, with the shape of 2026-10-23 (bind a log event or its metadata, then == on fields): haiku-1 lines 48-50, haiku-2 lines 77-80, sonnet-1 lines 104-106, sonnet-2 lines 87-89 (bound by assert_receive). opus-1 is clean: {result, log} = with_log(...) is the exempted destructure, and result and log are compared whole with the value under test on the left. charge/3 results are asserted with patterns (haiku-2, sonnet-1) or with the call on the left of == (haiku-1, sonnet-2) in every handler run. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5: one module per outcome in opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, one module answering by token in haiku-1.

Rules outside the list, graded on current text. "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" changed: a trailing keyword list may now stay inline, one option per line. That does not reach this sweep's one hit, haiku-2 lines 39-43, a multi-line handler config map inside a matched call, which the rule still names; no run spreads charge/3's options over several lines this time (each wraps the call in a one-line helper), so the 4 of 5 of 2026-10-23 falls to 1 of 5. "Use `do:` ..." (rewritten, but its sentence "when `mix format` moves it onto a line of its own, the body is too long for `do:`" is unchanged): haiku-2 line 118 and sonnet-1 line 72. "Read required keys ..." (first paragraph unchanged): sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read required metadata with meta[:key]; the meta[:pid] reads inside handler filters (haiku-1 line 29, sonnet-2 line 9) are not counted. "Before you finish" for the four unformatted lines. The new Readability rules (One expression per line, Name a step) and the rewritten pipeline, with, -> and capture rules find nothing: no pipeline, with, case or cond in any file; receive clauses (haiku-1 101-103, haiku-2 111-113, sonnet-1 66-68) hold one expression per body; gateway and message/format clauses form tables. Not reported, as before: comments above or inside handler modules (haiku-2 line 5, sonnet-1 lines 5-6, sonnet-2 lines 5-6), the explanatory comments in opus-1 (lines 4-5, 40) and haiku-1 (lines 8, 87-89), and gateway modules without @moduledoc false in an .exs script.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each with random seeds. Every file passed every time with no compiler warnings and no log line printed: opus-1 5 tests, haiku-1 7, haiku-2 7, sonnet-1 8, sonnet-2 9.
